claims.text: Depositing a 2D high-entropy-alloy-based tribofilm onto an untreated HEA surface reduces the coefficient of friction relative to the untreated alloy.
Depositing a 2D high-entropy-alloy-based tribofilm onto an untreated HEA surface reduces wear rate relative to the untreated alloy.
The tribofilm remains effective from room temperature to approximately 800 °C.
High-flux sputtering or chemical vapor deposition can produce the proposed thermally stable 2D HEA chalcogenide/oxide-containing film.
Sliding contact causes an in-situ protective tribofilm or tribolayer to form from the deposited coating.
The coating remains effective in normal atmospheric or mildly oxidative environments under moderate mechanical-component loads and sliding speeds.
A lamellar or nanostructured surface film maintains a low-shear sliding interface.
The surface film provides a barrier against high-temperature oxidation.
The surface film provides a physical barrier against wear-induced damage.
The high-entropy composition and 2D structure enable adaptive oxide or chalcogen compounds to form during frictional heating.
Stress-induced tribocatalytic activity of HEA chalcogenide nanoflakes facilitates self-lubricating behavior.
Adaptive oxide or chalcogen formation reduces adhesive wear across a wide temperature range.
The coating decreases coefficient of friction by approximately 30–40% relative to the untreated alloy.
The coating reduces wear rate by approximately one order of magnitude relative to the untreated alloy.
The predicted friction and wear improvements persist continuously from room temperature to 800 °C.
Untreated HEAs often have coefficients of friction exceeding 0.6 at elevated temperatures.
Untreated HEAs have wear rates approaching 10^-5 mm³/(N·m) at elevated temperatures.
Tribologically beneficial oxide films on untreated HEAs tend to degrade or spall, causing progressively higher friction and wear.
Temperatures above approximately 900 °C or extremely corrosive environments may degrade the adhered tribofilm.
Very high loads or impact conditions may exceed the protective capacity of the tribofilm.
